conbody.p: Every page is framed the same way: a narrow rail down the left and one top bar across the top, so the work itself gets the rest of the screen. The frame is the same inside a project and on the workspace's own pages (Projects, workspace settings, workspace runs, What's new and platform admin); only the rail's buttons change.

ul.li:
The top bar reads left to right: the workspace switcher, the project switcher, the search across every project, Help, the notification bell and the account menu.
Switch workspace: click the workspace's name for the list of your workspaces, workspace settings and runs, and creating a company workspace.
Switch project: click the project's name (it reads All projects on a workspace page) for the workspace's projects. Choose one to open it at its Summary; All projects opens the Projects page and + New project starts a project from wherever you are.

The rail inside a project has a button for each part of the project, in the order the work runs — Plan, Define, Verify and Agents — and links to Activity and Settings. Click a group to open its pages beside the rail (Plan holds Overview, Summary, Board, Gantt and Releases, for example), then click the page. The group holding the page you are on is marked. The list closes when you arrive, or with Esc or a click anywhere else.

The row under the top bar lists the pages of the group you are in, with the one you are reading underlined, so the page next door is one click away. It is where a page is named: the page itself does not repeat its name. Activity and Settings belong to no group, so they have no row.
The rail on a workspace page lists the workspace's own pages: Home, Runs (where the workspace has them), News (What's new), Admin for platform admins, and Settings.
Home is at the top of the rail on every page and opens the workspace's Home: what needs you across every project, the workspace's activity, and its projects to choose from.

conbody.p: On a phone there is no rail. On a workspace page the top bar holds the workspace switcher above the project switcher, with help, the bell and your account beside them. Inside a project the top bar names the project, and a bar along the bottom reads Home, Plan, Define, Verify, More from left to right: the same groups in the same order as the rail on a computer. A group's tab opens the page you last read in that group, and the row under the top bar lists the group's other pages (swipe it sideways when it is wider than the screen). More is the whole menu as a page of its own: the workspace switcher, the project switcher and the search, then every page as a tile under its group, Help for the page you were on, the Manual, All projects, and under You your account menu.
